rationale:
WHAT IS BROKEN. `load_page_sections_from_spec` is the single place the page-build pipeline assembles a page's section list (site_plan_sections -> site_specs.site_plan -> pages.sections -> same-role sibling). None of the four tiers reads `page_components`, so a section a human has LOCKED onto the live page that the plan does not name can never enter the list. Downstream, `save_page_sections` (DELETE all agent-writable rows + INSERT the proposal) finds the locked row absent from the proposal, exiles it to `len(sections)+1` and files a `lock_blocked_change ... blocked_action=remove` item -- EVERY pass. The 058 guard protects the ROW; nothing protected the LIST, and `pages.sections` kept telling every reader the section did not exist. Diagnosed by 090 run d9f97c15 (CONFIRMED at the assembler, after c199c4bf REFUTED the consumer framing). Owner ruling 2026-08-15: 'the improvement loop that tried to remove the chat box: CHECK AND FIX IT'.

MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED (2026-08-15, live DB): 26 locked page_components rows fleet-wide, all `permanent`, 0 with build_status='removed'; 13 sit on tier-1 pages whose plan omits them (webdesign.uk/contact `chat-input-box`, 12 loancalculator.co.uk calculators); 6 open `remove`-blocked items, FIVE filed that afternoon (17:11-17:48Z) by page-build-handler runs whose spec_sections came from tier 1 = [hero, ported-prose, faq, tool-cta]. Within two hours the tail-exile moved loancalculator `index/tool-3` from position 4 to 6 and `tool-settlement-calculator/tool-2` from 3 to 5. It is a framework class firing now, not one site.

THE FIX, IN ONE SENTENCE: after any tier has served, merge the page's non-agent-writable live rows into the list at their live position, classified by THE GUARD'S OWN predicate and paired by THE GUARD'S OWN matching arms, and give the one live check that compares plan-vs-cache the same merge so it does not start shouting drift on every fixed page.

WHY IN THE LOADER (candidate 1 of the bug file). It is the one chokepoint every build/rebuild path passes through, so the bad state (an assembled list missing a locked live section) becomes unrepresentable at the source. Candidate 2 (make every plan producer lock-aware) has multiple producers plus two legacy tiers it would never reach and does not close the door alone; candidate 3 (suppress save-side) is the guard's behaviour today and leaves the list and cache lying.

WHY datahelpers, AND WHY THE SAME PREDICATE. Two packages need the two pieces: the loader (`actions`) and `check_section_source_drift` (`actions/discovery_checks`); `actions` imports `discovery_checks` imports `datahelpers`, so shared code lives at the bottom. The lock arm of the new query is `NOT datahelpers.AgentWritableSQLFor("pc.")` -- the identical string the 058 DELETE and `loadActiveLockedRows` use -- never re-typed (LOCK-007's derived-predicate rule; LANDMINES 'the PIN predicate is not the POOL predicate'); a test refuses a `locked_at IS NOT NULL` lookalike. `NormalizeComponentFunction` moves down to datahelpers with a delegating wrapper in actions, so the merge and `matchLockedRow` normalise with one function.

WHY THE PAIRING MIRRORS matchLockedRow, ARM FOR ARM, CONSUME-ONCE. 'Already in the list' must mean the same thing to the loader and to the guard, or the loader adds an entry the guard then pairs with the SAME locked row's identity while inserting the fresh copy as a duplicate -- that is precisely how bugs_open/189 turned a locked calculator into two rows. Arms: slot exact -> slot kebab-normalised (the 041 snake_case landmine) -> component function/name (the list carries names not ids, so this stands in for the guard's identity arm; identity resolves later in plan_sections Path 0). Two locked rows rendering one component against a plan naming it once pair one and insert the other; against a plan naming it twice pair both.

WHY NOT WHEN NO TIER SERVED. A page with no plan anywhere but a locked row would get a list of ONLY its locked rows -- neither the plan nor the page -- and a rebuild on that list would DELETE the page's unlocked siblings (the prune floor would probably refuse the save, but a safety floor is not a design). Such a page keeps today's 'no sections' outcome; check_sectionless_pages owns it.

WHY ONE jsonb-COMPARED CACHE SYNC. The three per-tier syncs guarded on `sections::text IS DISTINCT FROM $1`, which is ALWAYS true (Postgres jsonb text prints `", "`, Go json.Marshal prints `","` -- verified live: text form distinct=t, jsonb form distinct=f), so every build rewrote pages.sections and bumped updated_at. Consolidated to one sync AFTER the merge, comparing jsonb, so the cache carries the merged list and an unchanged list is a genuine no-op. Tier 3 (which reads the cache) reaches it too -- a no-op unless the merge corrected the cache it read.

SCOPE / GOVERNANCE. This changes what a shared mechanism guarantees (the assembled list now = plan ∪ locked live rows), so I expect the architecture seat to look; I argue it RESTORES the guarantee the lock mechanism states (031_locks.md: 'Without locks, every human edit is fragile -- the next agent run reverts it') rather than adding new authority, and it is registered in the same commit (LOCK-008 + index row) per the 2026-07-28 ruling condition (2). 031_locks.md L156 ('don't merge locks across multiple tables in a downstream reader') is addressed head-on: the loader does not answer 'is this locked?' from two tables; it answers 'what sections does this page HAVE?', and page_components is a legitimate source for that. Consumers TOLD, not merely measured (owner ruling 2026-07-29 s3): page-build-handler is the loader's only live consumer (055); check_section_source_drift is changed with it (or it files one item per fixed page -- 13 on day one); save_sections_prune_floor's plan cohort (pages.sections length - locked rows) becomes exact instead of under-counting; readers that re-implement the tier order and STAY lock-blind by design are named in the file header and the register entry. Two corrections to the bug file itself are recorded (WRONG_CALLS): 282's resolver is NOT on this path (plan_sections never calls loadComponentNameResolver -- callers are validate_plan and apply_gap_plan; a merged slot resolves via plan_sections Path 0 by stored identity), and the proposal save diffs is the content WRITER's sections_metadata (render_component emits component_id + stored_slot_name, so the guard's identity/slot arms pair the merged entry: consume-and-keep, `overwrite` item, no duplicate).

STATE, PLAINLY: committed alongside this submission, NOT live (Go, inert until the next roll). Unit-proven and mutation-proven; the acceptance is the owner's five post-roll criteria in the bug file, run by the filing lane, and this bug stays OPEN until then.

edits.rationale: One query answering 'which rows on this page may automation NOT rewrite?' with the guard's own predicate negated — the identical string the 058 DELETE uses — plus a MEMBERSHIP filter (build_status <> 'removed', 0 rows today) stated separately. Exported SQL so a test pins the reuse. Site-wide variant for the discovery check (one query, not one per page).

Pure merge. Pairs each list entry with at most ONE locked row using save_page_sections.matchLockedRow's arms in order (slot exact → slot kebab → component function/name), consume-once; inserts unpaired rows at position-1 clamped to the tail, ascending. Mirroring the guard's arms is what prevents the 189 duplicate-row shape. Returns merged, inserted rows and their indices so the loader can keep section_facts aligned. NormalizeComponentFunction + IsKebabCase move down here; actions.NormalizeComponentFunction becomes a one-line delegate.

After tier assembly and ONLY when a tier served: load + merge; when tier 1 served insert nil into specSectionFacts at each insertedAt (else the len==len guard silently drops the whole fact-scoping payload); report locked_sections_merged/locked_merge_count; best-effort on query failure exactly as loadActiveLockedRows is (Warn, proceed unmerged — the guard still protects the row). Replace the three per-tier cache syncs with ONE after the merge, `sections IS DISTINCT FROM $1::jsonb` (the old text comparison was always true). Header documents source 5 and the no-tier rule.

The consumer that compares plan-vs-cache verbatim would file one section_source_drift item per fixed page (13 on day one). Load locked rows once per site (loud on failure — comparing raw lists would flag every locked page) and compare MergeLockedPageSlots(authoritative) vs MergeLockedPageSlots(cache): a locked live section is never drift by itself, a pre-fix cache is not either, a genuine one-store edit still is.

One normaliser for both packages: delegate to datahelpers.NormalizeComponentFunction; ValidateComponentFunction uses datahelpers.IsKebabCase. Same shape as pageComponentAgentWritableSQL → datahelpers.AgentWritableSQLFor. Behaviour unchanged (documented examples pinned in the datahelpers test).

Pins (1) the predicate reuse (contains `NOT `+AgentWritableSQLFor("pc."), refuses `locked_at IS NOT NULL`), (2) twelve merge cases: append at tail (contact chat box), insert at live position, clamp beyond tail, present-by-slot / kebab / function → no duplicate, consume-once with two rows of one component, two-rows-two-entries, two insertions ascending, slotless fallback, no rows, empty list; input not mutated; (3) the moved normaliser's documented examples.

plan.risks: (1) NOT LIVE until the next chassis roll; the acceptance is the owner's five criteria and cannot be run before it — the bug stays OPEN and the chat-box lock stays ON. (2) A merged in-list locked section now draws an `overwrite` lock_blocked_change item per pass instead of a `remove` one (058's design; deduped by item_key) — the fix stops the removal attempts and the lying cache, it does not make locked sections silent; the register entry names the carry-stored-row follow-up as an open question. (3) The merge restores MEMBERSHIP not HISTORY: rows already exiled to the tail by earlier passes stay at the tail until a human moves them or a replan names the component (then the plan position wins via the function arm). (4) The pairing's arm 3 uses component function/name where the guard uses component_id — the list has no ids; if a plan names a component's function while a DIFFERENT locked row renders that component under a positional slot, the merge treats it as present and the guard pairs by identity, which is the same outcome; but two locked rows of one component against a plan naming it once will insert the second — intended, and tested. (5) check_section_source_drift now fails LOUD if the locked-row query errors (previously it had no such dependency) — chosen because the alternative is a silent wave of false drift items. (6) The 'no tier served → no merge' rule leaves a page that has ONLY locked rows and no plan reading 'no sections' — today's behaviour, owned by check_sectionless_pages; stated in the header. (7) Best-effort on the loader's locked query failure means a DB hiccup produces one lock-blind build (Warn logged, guard still protects the row) — the same trade loadActiveLockedRows makes; a reviewer may prefer fail-loud here. (8) NormalizeComponentFunction moved packages; behaviour pinned by test but any caller relying on the old kebabCaseRe var name in actions no longer compiles — grep showed two uses, both updated.
